principles.principle: API-First Modular Monolith — two frontend clients served by a single NestJS backend from day one
principles.rationale: The mentee web app and admin portal are independent Next.js apps consuming the same NestJS backend via REST APIs. LTM evolutionary-scaling.md places this at Phase 2 (API-First) from launch because multiple clients exist immediately — not Phase 1 (server-rendered monolith). The backend is a modular monolith (not microservices), maximizing velocity within the €125k fixed budget and 16-week timeline while maintaining strong module boundaries for future service extraction. PP-6 level 3 (Market-Ready v1) and PP-3 level 5 (Multi-Sided Platform) together drive this choice: market-ready quality with multi-persona complexity.

principles.principle: TypeScript Full-Stack — unified type system across all deployment units
principles.rationale: Next.js (TypeScript), NestJS (TypeScript), and Prisma (TypeScript ORM) share type definitions for API contracts and domain models. A shared-types package eliminates frontend-backend integration bugs at compile time. Critical for a 16-week fixed-price engagement (Nagarro) where runtime type errors carry schedule and budget risk. LTM backend-nodejs.md recommends TypeScript for all new Node.js projects and specifically recommends NestJS for teams needing structured governance over 7+ integrations.

principles.principle: Stateless API Layer — JWT-based authentication, no server-side session affinity
principles.rationale: NestJS backend is stateless: all request context travels in JWT claims (user ID, role, Stripe Connect account reference, KeyCloak realm). Enables horizontal ECS Fargate task scaling without session affinity routing. JWT access tokens expire in 15 minutes; KeyCloak manages refresh token lifecycle. NFR-3 level 3 (Fast) + NFR-6 level 3 (Growth-Oriented) both require the backend to scale horizontally without state migration.

principles.principle: Event-Driven Async for Side Effects — BullMQ queues for all non-critical paths
principles.rationale: Email delivery (SendGrid), push notifications (FCM), Zoom recording webhook processing, payout scheduling, Elasticsearch mentor index sync, and recording TTL deletion are all async via BullMQ (Redis-backed job queue). API endpoints enqueue and return immediately; side effects execute in dedicated background worker processes. Prevents API p95 latency from being inflated by external service call latency. BullMQ is preferred over Kafka/RabbitMQ because Redis is already in the stack. LTM messaging-queues.md confirms Redis Streams / BullMQ is appropriate at MVP scale (< 10K initial users).

principles.principle: Config Captured at Booking Time — commission rate and cancellation policy versioned per session
principles.rationale: When a session is booked, the current commission rate (10-20%) and cancellation policy are captured in the session record. In-flight sessions retain their original config values. Admin portal config changes apply only to sessions booked after the change. Resolved OQ-5 from roadmap.yaml. Prevents retroactive financial recomputation and protects mentor payout expectations.

principles.principle: Multi-Store Deletion Orchestrator — GDPR right-to-deletion cascade as a first-class component
principles.rationale: GDPR right-to-deletion must cascade across: PostgreSQL (soft-delete PII, hard-delete after retention period), Elasticsearch (mentor profile index deletion), S3 (recording and artefact object deletion), Redis (cache key invalidation), SendGrid (contact suppression), and FCM (device token removal). ComplianceModule contains a DeletionOrchestrator service designed upfront to avoid multi-sprint refactoring when E8 ships. NFR-7 level 4 (Sensitive) and NFR-5 level 3 (Standard Compliance) both drive this architectural decision. Resolved CB-1 (per-session GDPR consent) and OQ-6 (TPDP).

principles.principle: Managed Services Over Self-Hosted — AWS managed offerings reduce operational burden for the fixed-budget team
principles.rationale: AWS RDS PostgreSQL, ElastiCache Redis, OpenSearch Service, and S3 are all fully managed. LTM search-engines.md explicitly warns: 'Elasticsearch for small teams without DevOps capacity — it's operationally complex to run and tune.' A small delivery team on a €125k fixed budget cannot sustain the operational overhead of self-managed database, cache, and search clusters. Managed services provide Multi-AZ availability, automated backups, and patch management at a cost that fits within the NFR-4 level 3 (Standard Availability) target of 99.5% uptime.

principles.principle: Dual Stripe Account Routing — INR and non-INR transactions on separate Stripe entities
principles.rationale: Indian domestic payment regulations require a separate Stripe India entity with INR settlement rails (distinct API keys, separate merchant account). The PaymentModule routes by currency: INR → Stripe India; USD/CHF/EUR → Stripe Global. Both accounts use Stripe Connect for mentor payouts. Resolved CB-2 and OQ-3 from roadmap.yaml. This dual-account architecture must be built into the PaymentModule from Sprint 1 — retrofitting currency routing is high-risk.

deployment_units.name: mentee-web-app
deployment_units.responsibility: Mentee-facing web application. Server-side rendered mentor discovery and profile pages for SEO indexability. Client-side rendered authenticated flows: session booking, payment confirmation, session history dashboard, in-app notification centre, and referral programme. Implements GDPR cookie consent banner and per-session recording consent gate at session join (CB-1 resolved).
deployment_units.communication: HTTPS REST to AWS API Gateway with JWT Bearer token in Authorization header. Stripe.js (client-side SDK) for Payment Intent confirmation without raw card data touching the platform. KeyCloak auth code flow (PKCE) for login and token exchange.

deployment_units.name: admin-portal
deployment_units.responsibility: Admin-facing SPA for platform operations: mentor onboarding approvals and verification artefact review, session oversight, financial operations (manual payouts, refund processing), dispute resolution (session recording access), quality monitoring (auto-flag queue), system configuration (commission rates, cancellation policies, pricing bands), analytics KPI dashboards, platform content management via Strapi.
deployment_units.communication: HTTPS REST to AWS API Gateway with JWT Bearer token carrying Admin role claim. NestJS AdminModule guards all admin-scoped routes with RBAC role guard. Read-only access to Strapi CMS REST API for content template management.

deployment_units.name: backend-api
deployment_units.responsibility: NestJS modular monolith. Single deployable containing 12 domain modules: AuthModule, UserModule, MarketplaceModule, SessionModule, PaymentModule, RatingsModule, AdminModule, CommsModule, ComplianceModule (DeletionOrchestrator), AnalyticsModule, ReferralModule, ConfigModule (commission rates, cancellation policies, pricing bands with version-at-capture).
deployment_units.communication: Receives HTTPS from API Gateway (internal VPC). Reads/writes PostgreSQL via Prisma ORM. Reads Redis via ioredis for caching and rate limiting. Writes BullMQ jobs to Redis for async side effects. Calls OpenSearch SDK for Elasticsearch operations. Calls AWS S3 SDK for recording and artefact storage. Calls Zoom REST API for meeting management. Calls KeyCloak Admin REST API for user provisioning and role assignment. Calls Stripe Node SDK for Payment Intents, Stripe Connect, and webhook validation.

deployment_units.name: background-workers
deployment_units.responsibility: BullMQ consumer processes running in a dedicated ECS Fargate task. Processes async jobs: EmailWorker (SendGrid templates), PushWorker (FCM web push), ZoomWebhookWorker (recording ready callbacks, S3 upload), PayoutScheduler (cron-driven post-session), RecordingTTLWorker (3-day S3 lifecycle deletion), SearchSyncWorker (mentor profile → OpenSearch index).
deployment_units.communication: Consumes BullMQ jobs from Redis (ElastiCache). Calls Twilio SendGrid REST API. Calls Firebase Admin SDK for FCM. Calls Zoom REST API for recording download and deletion. Calls AWS S3 SDK for recording lifecycle management. Writes payout records to PostgreSQL via Prisma. Updates OpenSearch mentor index via OpenSearch SDK.

deployment_units.name: keycloak
deployment_units.responsibility: Identity and Access Management: user registration (email + password), social login brokering (Google OAuth2, Apple Sign In), JWT issuance and validation (JWKS endpoint), RBAC realm roles (Mentee, Mentor, Admin), refresh token management, MFA capability (optional for admin role), single sign-on across web app and admin portal.
deployment_units.communication: Frontends redirect to KeyCloak for auth code flow (PKCE). API Gateway Lambda Authorizer validates JWT signatures against KeyCloak JWKS endpoint. NestJS AuthModule calls KeyCloak Admin REST API for programmatic user creation and role assignment.

deployment_units.name: strapi-cms
deployment_units.responsibility: Headless CMS for platform content: email notification HTML templates (session confirmation, payment receipt, dispute update, payout confirmation), help centre articles, terms and conditions, privacy policy, and platform content. Enables non-technical admin to update content without code deployments.
deployment_units.communication: NestJS CommsModule and AdminModule consume Strapi Content REST API over HTTPS. Content editors access Strapi admin panel directly via separate URL.

stack.purpose: SSR for mentor discovery and profile pages (SEO indexability); CSR for authenticated session flows
stack.rationale: Pre-decided in product.yaml delivery_context. LTM frontend-react-nextjs.md confirms: 'Choose when SSR/SSG for SEO matters for consumer-facing products (PP-7 = 2-4).' PP-1 level 4 (General Consumer) + PP-7 level 3 (Professional Services) = mentor profile pages need SSR for Google indexing. App Router enables per-route rendering strategy (SSR for discovery, CSR for authenticated flows).

stack.purpose: Utility-first styling and accessible component primitives for mentee-facing UI
stack.rationale: PP-1 level 4 (General Consumer) and PP-2 level 3 (Multi-Channel Responsive) demand polished, accessible UI with responsive layouts. shadcn/ui provides Radix UI-based accessible components (dialogs, dropdowns, forms) as copy-paste code — no opaque dependency. QP-6 level 2 (Basic Accessibility) is met by Radix UI's ARIA compliance.

stack.purpose: Server state management, API data caching, background refresh, and optimistic updates for booking flows
stack.rationale: PP-5 level 3 (Bidirectional integrations) means the UI needs real-time-ish data freshness for session status, payment confirmation, and notification counts. TanStack Query handles cache invalidation, loading states, and error boundaries without global state complexity.

stack.purpose: Client-side Payment Intent confirmation and card element rendering without raw card data touching platform
stack.rationale: PCI DSS compliance requires card data to be handled entirely by Stripe's client-side SDK. Stripe Elements renders PCI-compliant card capture UI in an iframe. The backend creates Payment Intents; Stripe.js confirms client-side. NFR-2 level 3 (Business Grade) mandates PCI DSS tokenisation.

stack.purpose: Admin SPA for platform operations — no SSR needed (not public-facing, no SEO requirement)
stack.rationale: Consistent with mentee-web-app stack (shared Next.js expertise). LTM frontend-react-nextjs.md notes: 'Avoid SSR for purely client-side SPAs where SEO doesn't matter (admin dashboards, internal tools).' Admin portal uses Next.js App Router with 'use client' components dominant.

stack.purpose: Data-dense admin tables (mentor list, session queue, payout queue) and analytics chart components
stack.rationale: PP-3 level 5 (Multi-Sided Platform) means the admin portal has complex tabular data (dispute queues, financial dashboards, quality monitoring). TanStack Table provides headless table primitives with sorting, filtering, and pagination. Recharts provides composable React chart components for the E9 analytics dashboards.

stack.purpose: Structured backend framework providing module system, dependency injection, decorators, and middleware for the modular monolith
stack.rationale: Node.js confirmed in product.yaml (I-02 resolved). LTM backend-nodejs.md recommends NestJS for teams needing structured governance over complex codebases. 10+ domain modules with 7+ external integrations justify NestJS's governance overhead over Express or Fastify. TypeScript-first with native OpenAPI (Swagger) generation. Node 20 LTS is the current long-term support release.

stack.purpose: High-performance HTTP request handling replacing NestJS's default Express adapter
stack.rationale: Fastify delivers 2-3x higher throughput than Express for I/O-bound API workloads. NFR-3 level 3 (Fast) requires < 500ms p95. Fastify's schema-based validation (JSON Schema) aligns with NestJS's DTO/ValidationPipe pattern. NestJS Fastify adapter is production-stable and recommended for performance-sensitive APIs.

stack.purpose: Type-safe database client for PostgreSQL with migrations, schema management, and generated TypeScript types
stack.rationale: Prisma generates TypeScript types from the schema, providing compile-time type safety for all database queries. Prisma Migrate handles schema versioning and deployment. NFR-7 level 4 (Sensitive) benefits from type-safe queries reducing SQL injection risk.

stack.purpose: DTO validation decorators for all NestJS controller inputs; transforms raw request body to typed DTO instances
stack.rationale: NestJS's ValidationPipe with class-validator is the standard NestJS validation pattern. TP2 (TypeScript Full-Stack) is reinforced by having validated DTOs at the API boundary. QP-2 level 3 (Enforced Standards) requires input validation on all endpoints.

stack.purpose: JWT bearer token validation against KeyCloak JWKS endpoint for all protected routes
stack.rationale: KeyCloak is pre-decided as the IAM provider. Passport-keycloak-bearer handles JWT validation by fetching KeyCloak's JWKS public keys. NestJS guards wrap Passport strategies for route-level RBAC. Standard approach for NestJS + KeyCloak integration per LTM security-infrastructure.md.

stack.purpose: Redis-backed job queue for async side effects: email delivery, push notifications, Zoom webhook processing, payout scheduling, search sync, recording TTL
stack.rationale: TP4 (Event-Driven Async) mandates a job queue. BullMQ is built on top of Redis, which is already in the stack (LTM messaging-queues.md: 'Redis Streams / BullMQ: built into Redis — appropriate for MVP scale'). BullMQ provides job retry, rate limiting, priority queues, delayed jobs (payout scheduling), and per-job progress tracking.

stack.purpose: Explicit state machine for session lifecycle with 8 states and transition guards (requested → accepted → scheduled → active → completed/cancelled/disputed/expired)
stack.rationale: E3 feasibility identifies session state machine as high-risk: 'state bugs can leave sessions in inconsistent states.' XState provides auditable state transitions, guards, and side effects as explicit declarations. The session state machine is complex enough (8 states, multiple transition triggers including webhooks) to warrant a formal FSM library over ad-hoc boolean flags.

stack.technology: PostgreSQL 16 (AWS RDS Multi-AZ, db.t3.medium, 1 read replica)
stack.purpose: Primary relational data store for all transactional data: users, mentor profiles, sessions, payments, ratings, referrals, notifications, audit trail
stack.rationale: LTM relational.md: 'Financial operations and ACID guarantees mandate PostgreSQL.' E4 (Payment Processing), E5 (Ratings/Disputes), and E6 (Admin Operations) all require ACID transactions for financial data integrity. PostgreSQL 16 on AWS RDS Multi-AZ provides automated failover (< 60s RTO) meeting NFR-4 level 3 availability.

stack.purpose: API response caching for mentor search results, session-level caching, rate limit counters, BullMQ job queue backend
stack.rationale: Pre-decided in product.yaml (NFR-3 rationale). LTM nosql-keyvalue.md confirms Redis for 'session caching, rate limiting, real-time counters, search result caching.' Redis 7.x on ElastiCache provides managed, Multi-AZ Redis with automatic failover. Dual-purpose: API cache + BullMQ backing store eliminates need for a separate queue broker.

stack.technology: AWS OpenSearch Service 2.11 (1x t3.medium.search node, managed)
stack.purpose: Full-text mentor search with category, geography, and pricing filters; mentor discovery and recommendation ranking
stack.rationale: Elasticsearch pre-decided in product.yaml (E2 architecture impact). LTM search-engines.md: 'When content volume exceeds database full-text search capability and for e-commerce/content discovery.' AWS OpenSearch Service (managed Elasticsearch-compatible) eliminates self-hosted operational burden. TP7 (Managed Services) drives this choice.

stack.purpose: Session recording storage (3-day TTL via S3 Lifecycle rules), mentor verification artefact storage (indefinite retention), and uploaded profile media
stack.rationale: E3 and E8 require secure, reliable storage with TTL enforcement for recordings. S3 Lifecycle rules implement the 3-day recording deletion automatically (OQ-7 resolved). S3 is the natural choice when backend is on AWS ECS — same account, IAM policies for admin-only access via signed URLs, server-side encryption (SSE-S3) satisfying NFR-7 level 4.

stack.technology: Strapi 5.x (self-hosted on ECS Fargate, db.t3.micro PostgreSQL)
stack.purpose: Email notification templates, help centre articles, platform terms and privacy policy content management
stack.rationale: Pre-decided in product.yaml (E6 architecture impact: 'Strapi CMS as third persistence layer'). Strapi 5.x provides a content REST API and admin panel. Self-hosted on ECS Fargate (separate task) to keep it within the AWS infrastructure boundary. Uses its own small PostgreSQL instance to avoid schema coupling with the main application database.

stack.technology: KeyCloak 24.x (self-hosted on ECS Fargate, db.t3.small PostgreSQL)
stack.purpose: User registration, login, social login brokering (Google OAuth2, Apple Sign In), JWT issuance, RBAC realm roles, MFA
stack.rationale: Pre-decided in product.yaml scope and NFR rationale. KeyCloak is the enterprise-grade IAM solution supporting all required auth flows. Self-hosted on ECS Fargate within the same AWS account — avoids vendor lock-in for a security-critical component and keeps PII (user credentials) under platform control. KeyCloak 24.x is the current stable release with active security support.

stack.purpose: Container build and serverless container orchestration for backend-api, background-workers, keycloak, and strapi
stack.rationale: Product.yaml QP4 rationale confirms Docker containerisation. LTM containerization.md: 'AWS ECS Fargate removes the need to manage EC2 instances — pay per task, auto-scaling, IAM task roles.' ECS Fargate is preferred over EKS (Kubernetes) at this scale. Kubernetes is LTM anti-pattern for teams < 5 engineers on MVP budgets.

stack.technology: GitHub Actions (multi-stage: lint → typecheck → test → build → deploy)
stack.purpose: Automated testing, container builds, and deployments to dev/staging/production environments
stack.rationale: Pre-decided in product.yaml (QP4 rationale). LTM ci-cd.md: 'GitHub Actions — integrated with GitHub, marketplace plugins, generous free tier.' QP-4 level 3 (Continuous Delivery) requires automated pipelines for all environments. GitHub Actions native integration with GitHub repository (Nagarro delivery) eliminates external CI setup.

stack.purpose: Secure storage and rotation for all API keys: Stripe India key, Stripe Global key, Zoom OAuth credentials, SendGrid API key, FCM service account JSON, KeyCloak admin credentials
stack.rationale: TP2 principle mandates no credentials in source code or environment variables committed to git. QP-7 level 3 (SAST + Dependencies) includes secret scanning in CI. AWS Secrets Manager integrates natively with ECS task role IAM — containers receive secrets at runtime via IAM without storing them in environment variables.

stack.purpose: SAST scanning on every PR for security vulnerabilities; ESLint enforces coding standards; Prettier enforces formatting
stack.rationale: QP-7 level 3 (SAST + Dependencies) and QP-2 level 3 (Enforced Standards) drive this. CodeQL is GitHub-native (no additional cost with GitHub Advanced Security). ESLint with typescript-eslint ruleset enforces TypeScript best practices. Prettier eliminates formatting debates. Pre-commit hooks via Husky + lint-staged enforce standards before push.

stack.purpose: Automated dependency vulnerability scanning with auto-generated PRs for security patches
stack.rationale: QP-7 level 3 (SAST + Dependencies) explicitly includes dependency scanning. Dependabot provides automatic security advisory monitoring and PR generation for vulnerable dependencies across both JavaScript/TypeScript packages. npm audit in CI pipeline blocks builds with high-severity vulnerabilities.

stack.purpose: Declarative infrastructure provisioning for ECS clusters, RDS, ElastiCache, OpenSearch, S3, API Gateway, and IAM roles
stack.rationale: LTM iac.md: 'Declarative IaC ensures reproducible environments and enables blue-green deployments.' QP-4 level 3 (Continuous Delivery) requires multiple environments (dev/staging/prod) with consistent configuration. Both CloudFormation and Terraform provide the required state management and diff-before-apply workflow.

platforms.purpose: Centralised IAM for all three personas (Mentee, Mentor, Admin); JWT issuance and validation; social login brokering
platforms.rationale: Pre-decided. Enterprise-grade open-source IAM with RBAC, OIDC, social login brokering (Google, Apple), and MFA. Self-hosted on ECS Fargate for PII control. NFR-2 level 3 (Business Grade) security posture requires centralised IAM with MFA capability.

platforms.platform: Stripe (Stripe India account + Stripe Global account + Stripe Connect)
platforms.purpose: Payment Intent-based escrow capture, multi-currency processing, mentor payout via Connect, refund processing
platforms.rationale: Pre-decided (I-04 resolved). Stripe supports all 4 target currencies (INR, USD, CHF, EUR), provides Payment Intents for escrow-compatible delayed capture, and Stripe Connect for mentor payouts. Dual account architecture (CB-2 resolved): Stripe India entity for INR domestic transactions, Stripe Global for other currencies. PCI DSS compliance via client-side Stripe.js tokenisation.

platforms.purpose: Transactional email delivery for session confirmations, payment receipts, booking reminders, dispute updates, payout confirmations
platforms.rationale: Pre-decided in product.yaml scope. SendGrid provides reliable transactional email with domain authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), delivery analytics, and template management integrating with Strapi CMS content. Domain authentication must be configured in Sprint 1 as per E7 feasibility note.

platforms.platform: Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) — web push, MVP scope
platforms.purpose: Web push notifications for session reminders, booking status updates, and dispute notifications on the mentee web app
platforms.rationale: Pre-decided in product.yaml scope. FCM provides web push notifications for browser-based notifications on the mentee web app. Mobile app is out of MVP scope, so native FCM mobile push is deferred to Phase 2. Firebase Admin SDK integrates with the NestJS background worker for server-side push dispatch.

platforms.purpose: Headless CMS for email notification templates, help centre articles, platform terms and privacy policy
platforms.rationale: Pre-decided in product.yaml (E6 architecture impact). Strapi enables non-technical content editors to update notification templates and help centre content without code deployments. REST Content API consumed by NestJS CommsModule and AdminModule. Self-hosted on ECS Fargate to avoid SaaS cost overhead at MVP scale.

platforms.purpose: Platform observability: API metrics, error rates, latency histograms, distributed tracing, and operational alerting
platforms.rationale: QP-5 level 3 (Monitored) and NFR-1 level 3 (Balanced Risk) require monitoring and alerting. AWS CloudWatch is cloud-native for ECS Fargate (no additional infrastructure), integrates with AWS X-Ray for distributed tracing across API Gateway → NestJS → RDS. TP7 (Managed Services) drives the CloudWatch-first choice over self-hosted Grafana stack.

platforms.purpose: Full-text mentor search with category, geography, and pricing filters; mentor discovery ranking
platforms.rationale: Pre-decided (Elasticsearch confirmed in product.yaml). AWS OpenSearch Service is the fully managed Elasticsearch-compatible service. LTM search-engines.md anti-pattern: 'Do not self-host Elasticsearch for small teams.' TP7 (Managed Services) and E2 architecture impact both mandate managed Elasticsearch. Index alias strategy enables zero-downtime reindexing.

technical_risks.risk: Stripe dual-account routing complexity — INR vs USD/CHF/EUR routing logic and dual Stripe Connect architectures must be built from Sprint 1; retrofitting adds high regression risk to the payment system
technical_risks.mitigation: Design PaymentModule with a CurrencyRouter service from day one that selects the correct Stripe client based on session currency. Implement idempotency keys on all Stripe API calls to prevent double-charges on network retries. Unit test both routing paths with Stripe test mode before any production transactions. Dual webhook handlers for both Stripe accounts with shared processing logic.

technical_risks.risk: Stripe Payment Intent delayed-capture 7-day limit — sessions booked more than 7 days in advance require re-authorization before capture; failed re-auth leaves session in limbo
technical_risks.mitigation: Implement a PayoutScheduler BullMQ worker that checks for Payment Intents approaching the 7-day capture window 24 hours before expiry. If re-authorization fails, notify mentee and mentor, cancel the session, and refund the authorization hold. SessionModule state machine must include a payment_expired terminal state.

technical_risks.risk: GDPR per-session recording consent gate (E3) — both parties must consent before Zoom recording activates; implementation requires frontend consent gate + backend enforcement + audit trail; any gap creates GDPR liability
technical_risks.mitigation: Session join flow: frontend renders consent modal with explicit Accept/Decline buttons before joining the Zoom meeting URL. Backend records consent timestamp, IP, and user ID in PostgreSQL audit table. Zoom recording is not activated until both parties have consented and backend has recorded consent. Consent records are retained even after session deletion (legal basis documentation).

technical_risks.risk: GDPR right-to-deletion cascade across 6 data stores (PostgreSQL, OpenSearch, S3, Redis, SendGrid, FCM) — any missed store creates GDPR violation; cascade failures must be retried without data inconsistency
technical_risks.mitigation: DeletionOrchestrator in ComplianceModule implements a saga pattern: each deletion step is recorded in a deletion_log table in PostgreSQL before execution. Steps are idempotent. Failed steps are retried via BullMQ with exponential backoff. Full deletion cascade (excluding financial audit trail retained 7 years for compliance) completes within 30 days per GDPR Article 17.

technical_risks.risk: Zoom Server-to-Server OAuth expiry — OAuth tokens expire and must be refreshed; recording webhook validation must be robust against replay attacks
technical_risks.mitigation: NestJS SessionModule implements a ZoomTokenService that refreshes OAuth tokens before expiry (cached in Redis with TTL). Zoom webhook Secret Token validation (HMAC-SHA256 header check) enforced on every inbound webhook. Replay protection via webhook event timestamp check (reject events older than 30 minutes).

technical_risks.risk: OpenSearch index sync lag — mentor profile updates may take up to 5 seconds to reflect in search results; admin-approved mentor may not appear immediately in search
technical_risks.mitigation: SearchSyncWorker processes index update jobs with low BullMQ priority for profile updates, high priority for profile activations (new admin-approved mentors). Add approximate sync delay disclaimer in admin portal. Implement manual reindex trigger in AdminModule for urgent corrections. Use OpenSearch index aliases for zero-downtime full reindexing.

technical_risks.risk: KeyCloak self-hosted availability — KeyCloak ECS task failure breaks all authentication across both frontends; no auth = full platform outage
technical_risks.mitigation: KeyCloak runs with minimum 2 ECS Fargate tasks behind an Application Load Balancer. API Gateway JWT Lambda Authorizer caches JWKS public keys (15-minute cache TTL), allowing short-duration tolerance of KeyCloak unavailability for existing authenticated sessions. Monitor KeyCloak health with CloudWatch alarms and immediate PagerDuty alert on task failure.

technical_risks.risk: NestJS background worker BullMQ job loss — if the ECS worker task crashes with in-flight jobs, BullMQ jobs may be lost unless lock expiry is configured correctly
technical_risks.mitigation: BullMQ configured with job retention (completed and failed jobs kept 24h) and automatic job retry with exponential backoff (3 retries). Set BullMQ lock duration to 60 seconds for long-running jobs (payout processing, recording upload). Failed jobs after max retries generate CloudWatch metric alarms for manual investigation.

technical_risks.risk: Prisma connection pool exhaustion under ECS autoscaling — each new ECS task opens a connection pool; rapid horizontal scaling creates PostgreSQL connection limit breaches
technical_risks.mitigation: Set Prisma connection_limit to 10 per task (not default). For peak scaling scenarios, evaluate PgBouncer as a connection pooler sitting between ECS tasks and RDS. CloudWatch metric for RDS DatabaseConnections with alarm at 80% of max_connections. RDS instance class (db.t3.medium) supports up to 1000 connections.

technical_risks.risk: Apple Sign In requires paid Apple Developer Program enrollment — missing credential blocks social login for iOS Safari users
technical_risks.mitigation: Ensure Apple Developer Program enrollment is completed before Sprint 1 development begins. Apple Sign In configuration in KeyCloak requires Apple private key, Key ID, and Team ID. Document as a prerequisite in the Sprint 0 setup checklist. Google OAuth2 is available as fallback social login if Apple Sign In setup is delayed.

technical_risks.risk: SendGrid domain authentication setup lag — SPF, DKIM, DMARC DNS propagation takes 24-72 hours; email deliverability poor without domain auth
technical_risks.mitigation: Domain authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) DNS configuration is a Sprint 0 prerequisite per E7 feasibility note. Felly Club platform domain must be ready before Sprint 1. Mock SendGrid delivery during Sprint 1-8 using SendGrid sandbox mode; replace with authenticated production delivery before E7 ships.

deployment.purpose: Vercel provides native Next.js SSR deployment with automatic CDN distribution, preview deployments per PR branch (QA without separate hosting), and Edge Network for static asset caching. Frontend-first platform appropriate for Next.js (LTM vercel.md confirms). Vercel handles Next.js-specific concerns (ISR, image optimization, Edge Middleware).

Same Vercel organisation as mentee-web-app. Separate Vercel project for access control isolation. Admin portal preview deployments use staging API Gateway endpoint; production uses production API Gateway. Consistent deployment workflow across both frontend applications.

deployment.platform: AWS ECS Fargate (us-east-1 primary, 2 tasks minimum)
deployment.purpose: Serverless container orchestration — no EC2 instance management. ECS task role provides IAM access to RDS, ElastiCache, OpenSearch, S3, and Secrets Manager. Fargate spot instances for non-production environments (cost reduction). Application Load Balancer routes traffic across tasks. Health check endpoint: GET /health.

Separate ECS service from backend-api for resource isolation — worker tasks consume different memory/CPU profiles (spike-based vs steady request handling). BullMQ consumers run as long-lived processes, not suitable for serverless functions. Separate deployment allows independent scaling of async processing capacity.

deployment.platform: AWS ECS Fargate (us-east-1, 2 tasks behind ALB)
deployment.purpose: Self-hosted for PII control — user credentials and auth tokens never leave AWS account. 2 tasks behind Application Load Balancer for high availability. KeyCloak uses its own small RDS PostgreSQL instance (db.t3.small) in the same VPC. HTTPS via ACM certificate on ALB.

Low-traffic content management workload — single Fargate task is sufficient. Strapi admin panel access restricted to admin VPN or IP allowlist. Separate small RDS PostgreSQL instance (db.t3.micro) to avoid schema coupling.

Primary relational data store. Multi-AZ provides automatic failover with < 60s RTO. 1 read replica in same AZ for analytics query isolation. Automated backups with 7-day retention. Encryption at rest via RDS storage encryption.

deployment.platform: AWS ElastiCache for Redis (Redis 7.x, cache.t3.micro, Multi-AZ with automatic failover)
deployment.purpose: API response caching, BullMQ job queue, and rate limit counters. ElastiCache Multi-AZ provides automatic failover. In-transit and at-rest encryption enabled. Cluster mode disabled at MVP scale (single primary + replica is sufficient).

Managed Elasticsearch-compatible service. Single t3.medium.search node appropriate for MVP mentor catalog size (hundreds of profiles). Encryption at rest and in transit. VPC deployment — no public endpoint. Scale to multi-node cluster when catalog grows.

Two S3 buckets: (1) felly-recordings — session recordings with 3-day lifecycle rule, SSE-S3 encryption, no public access, IAM policy restricts signed URL generation to AdminModule role only. (2) felly-artefacts — mentor verification documents, permanent retention, SSE-S3, IAM policy allows backend-api read/write.

observability.tracing: AWS X-Ray with NestJS OpenTelemetry SDK (aws-xray-sdk-node) — traces all inbound API requests through API Gateway → NestJS modules → RDS/ElastiCache/OpenSearch/S3 calls. Distributed trace IDs propagated via X-Amzn-Trace-Id header. Sampling rate: 5% in production, 100% for error traces.
metrics: API Gateway p50/p95/p99 latency per endpoint
ECS task CPU and memory utilization (alarm at 80%)
BullMQ job queue depth per queue (failed jobs alarm at > 10)
Stripe webhook delivery failure rate (via Stripe dashboard webhook logs)
SendGrid email delivery rate and bounce rate (via SendGrid Activity API)
S3 recording deletion success rate (RecordingTTLWorker job completion)
Payment processing success rate per currency (INR vs USD/CHF/EUR)
Session state machine transition error rate (invalid state transitions)
KeyCloak authentication success/failure rate (login errors alarm)
observability.logging: Structured JSON logging via Pino (NestJS Pino Logger integration). All log lines include: trace_id, user_id (hashed for PII), endpoint, duration_ms, status_code, and correlation_id. Logs shipped to AWS CloudWatch Logs via ECS Firelens log router. Log levels: ERROR (always), WARN (always), INFO (in production), DEBUG (dev/staging only). Financial operation logs tagged with financial=true for dedicated CloudWatch Insights queries and 7-year retention policy. GDPR-sensitive fields (email, name, IP) masked in logs via Pino redaction paths.
